title: Is this appealing enough? I lost my job to pay for more art.
author: xcantene
selftext:
I have been working hard on my multi-player monster hunting card game that works on desktop and mobile directly on your browser. 

The game was first intended to be a physical copy and I was working and designing everything with some artists. I then lost my job 3 months ago. I already had crappy digital demo that I was using mostly to balance my cards and use bots to test decks. It was miles away from this in fact you can still checkout how it looks as i have not released this new update as i dont feel people really care about the game. 

https://huntprotocol.cloudwanderstudios.com/

I have 10 years of experience as UX and Product Designer and I have not been able to land a single interview just yet. It seems AI is really replacing me. So I decided to push on my game after some encouragement from friends and even the artists working on the game. I put a lot of effort on a better UI with plenty of animations to make the card game more interesting and also having help from some VAs for free. 

I am still missing a lot of sound effects that I have to make. I love making these kind of stuff as I hate how AI makes sound effects. So my question to you as I show some of the gameplay and mobile UI. Is this something you consider appealing enough?

 I feel ashamed having to use AI imagines to fully fill up the missing art from monsters and some attacks but all icons and frames were design by me and a good chunk of the hunters with cards were fully made by artists. 

I did made a funding part on the game where people can see what art is placeholder and to help us fund the art that way everyone is aware how much I pay for each of these arts. 

Idk i feel very unsure of my game... if you want to check it out I can share a demo link with its password.

comments.author: Cold_for_Teacher
comments.body: The menu is a 1 to 1 copy of Legend of Runeterra's, up to the loading screen

replies.author: xcantene
replies.body:
If my game reminded you to LoR then that is a big compliment but I would invite you to take a second look at LoR as i have been carefully trying to not replicate and use as much as I can in the sense of good UX and avoid their UX issues with navigation. Their menu is a cluster mess at this point which is what I am trying to avoid. 

Just because I have a side menu like many other games does not make it a 1v1 copy. Anyways thank you for your comment :)

replies.author: cheyumaama
replies.body: Yeah AI copies from these templates that everyone used to use

comments.author: xcantene
comments.body: This is a really good point and thank you for catching it. There is a looot that sometimes AI tends to put extra and annoys me so I am always proof reading. For now I have been focusing on the cards. I decided to remove those suggestions of decks and tips as they are really not needed. If the ability of the card needs extra explanation then I failed at that design because I want this game to work also on physical. So thank you for pointing this out!

comments.author: Prestigious_Fee_2468
comments.body: It really don't matter how we think about it because what matters the most is the audience ur targeting. Personally I like the presentation, the formation, the way it's built, the battling looks pretty good. It's definitely something I'd try and I'm not even into card games outside of FF8. Definitely keep updating it with new content, if it's a free to play game I'd love to try it, is it on steam?
